obernants.approximation_semantics: Mathematical target with bounded finite evidence, not a proof.
obernants.assumptions: Ordinary Rust execution, sufficient allocation, byte equality.
obernants.domain: All finite byte slices and returned usize vector observations.
obernants.operator: Universe: finite byte inputs paired with arbitrary pairs of usize vectors. Excluded outputs have wrong lengths, zero odd radii, out-of-range spans, unequal symmetric byte pairs in a claimed span, or a radius whose next valid outer pair still matches. The model describes excluded behavior independently of negative tests.

obernants.approximation_semantics: Mathematical target with bounded finite evidence, not a proof.
obernants.assumptions: Ordinary Rust execution, sufficient allocation, byte equality.
obernants.domain: All finite byte slices and returned usize vector observations.
obernants.operator: Given two radius vectors of equal length n, compatible inputs are exactly byte strings of length n satisfying 1<=odd[i]<=min(i+1,n-i) and 0<=even[i]<=min(i,n-i), every symmetric equality inside every claimed span, and inequality of the next outer byte pair whenever that pair exists. Empty vectors admit empty input. Inconsistent equalities/inequalities admit no input; injective symbol relabelings exhibit nonunique antecedents.

obernants.operator: Injective byte relabeling preserves both vectors. A constant string has odd[i]=min(i+1,n-i), even[i]=min(i,n-i). UTF-8 bytes need not share the character-level palindrome structure.

obernants.approximation_semantics: Exact mathematical target under assumptions; bounded executed evidence only.
obernants.assumptions: Ordinary successful Rust execution, sufficient allocation and exact byte equality. Mathematical sums; test sums fit usize. Finite fixtures do not establish unrestricted correctness.
obernants.domain: Radius vectors of common length n<=256, byte witnesses.
obernants.observation_scope: Named relations and bounded source correspondence fixtures.
obernants.operator: Require 1<=o[i]<=min(i+1,n-i), 0<=e[i]<=min(i,n-i). Union symmetric pairs in both parities and add inequality edges for next outer pairs when in bounds. Feasible iff no edge collapses to one class; distinct class bytes construct a witness. Larger n additionally requires 256-colorability; the bounded routine does not decide this.

obernants.operator: Let L=b-a,c=a+floor(L/2). Palindrome membership iff L even and e[c]>=L/2, or L odd and o[c]>=floor(L/2)+1. Complete radii encode every nonempty interval's membership, not bytes.
